en: Bhūtirāja: Homage to Śiva, who bestows the absolute liberation consisting of all auspiciousness—Śiva, who is the sun that has quelled the darkness of the entire path of worldly existence, and who is the realization of one's own consciousness. (1)
I bow to the supreme Śiva, who is free from the distinctions of all modes of perception, who is to be known through self-awareness, and who abides in his own nature. //2//
Salutations be to Śambhu, who destroys the flood of conceptual constructions and the web of mental fabrications, and who transcends the state of supreme bliss. //3//

Victorious are the feet of Śambhu, which bestow the discernment between the essence and the non-essence of the boundless saṃsāra, and which are the causes for the awakening of the knowledge of absolute liberation (kaivalya). //4//
We worship that which is to be meditated upon, by seeing which the mind, intellect, ego, vital breaths, and the life-force of the subtle elements and senses turn away. //5//
I bow to pure consciousness, the unique small sword that severs the heart-knot of "mine" and "I," which devours both the active and the inactive. //6//
How can there be a description of reality (tattva) which is devoid of designation?
If it is somehow accessible through the logic of self-cognition (svasaṃvedana), [then how can it be described]? //7//
For one who lacks internal confidence through the instruction on the yoga of knowledge, how can there be the fruit of the supreme good, given the absence of such confidence? (8)

This state of wakefulness regarding one's own awakening is the means for attaining the goal; because of this wakefulness regarding one's own awakening, the sage abides in a state free from conceptual differentiation. //9//
There is no other means whatsoever than following one's own true being;
the yogi who follows that very [being] remains established in his own nature and shall become happy. 10.
Through the reflection upon his own volition, by resorting to pure gnosis, and from the attainment of supreme bliss, the sage attains the state of being a single mass of awakening. //11//
When one's own volition is restrained, the power abides within the possessor of power;
this identity of power and the possessor of power is the goal to be attained by yogis. //12//
When the knowledge of one's true nature has been attained, when the sheath of reality has been cast off, and when the cause of exertion has been scattered, he is indeed said to be liberated. //13//
One should maintain the grasp with a well-awakened mind upon mere awareness, until, by its own power, it becomes established in itself and solitary. //14//
Being ever perfectly awakened, one perceives the Self by means of the self;
for one who is established in the true nature of the seer, what else remains? //15//
Constant and perfect awakening—this alone is the destruction of the mind.
Through its destruction, yogis attain complete and direct realization. //16//

But he who, having turned back from [external objects], abides in self-awareness through non-duality, is the sovereign of those engaged in yoga and the sun that dispels the darkness of ignorance. //17//
For me, whose inner organ has been stilled, what remains to be attained here? The moon of my state transcends the bliss of experiencing one's own essential nature. //18//

For one in whom the firm and perfectly clear repose in the thorough cognition of one's own nature is established, and who is thus liberated from mental activity, absolute isolation shall soon be attained. (19)

For yogins whose minds are solely intent on setting aside the impressions of the grasped object and the act of grasping, and who are established in their own true self, the fortune of liberation is not difficult to attain. //20//
Rest in my own true nature has been attained; the succession of afflictions has ceased;
the state of subject and object is shattered; I am established, remaining firmly rooted in my own true nature. //21//
Whether he has emerged from meditation or remains restrained, he who attains the state of experiencing the essential nature of the awakening to non-dual consciousness is a knower of reality. //22//
For one whose self-abiding is never lost in any state whatsoever, what indeed can the delusions of wandering through the scriptures do? (23)

The yogi, whose self is liberated from the delusion born of the confusion between existence and non-existence through the dissolution of the conceptual constructions of "is" and "is not," remains forever free from fear even while living in the midst of people. //24//

By that yogi who has accomplished his purpose, through whom this samādhi—which dispenses with the instruments of action—has been practiced even once, the supreme [reality] has been directly realized. //25//
Having grasped myself within my own self without confusion through my own effort, I shall become awakened and established in my own nature, until I possess the splendor of Sadāśiva. //26//

The yogi, whose mental activity regarding all objects has been cast aside and who is partless in his mode of being, having once for all attained his gain within his own self, intent solely upon perfect awakening and established in himself, indeed casts off his own sheath. //27//

For one who possesses constant verbal expression, experience, and sound reasoning within their own self-awareness, it is appropriate to provide instruction and bring about the perfect awakening of disciples. //28//

Through the state of homelessness, through self-awakening, through the relinquishing of hope and pride, and through the severing of the path of existence and non-existence, there is no further assumption of a physical body. //29//

With an inwardly comforted mind, with diminished conceptualization, delighting in the attainment of his true nature, and satisfied by the nectar of his own experience, he reaches liberation, having fulfilled his purpose. //30//

Thus, for the attainment of the goal, I have described the accomplishment of one's own awakening—the true, stainless illuminator of consciousness that gives rise to the glory of absolute liberation (kaivalya). 31.

What indeed could one who has mastered many scriptures accomplish with that instruction which does not lead to the attainment of what was previously unattained and which is fully free from the fault of doubt? (32)

I bow to Śiva, who is taught by the mouth of the Guru; he who has performed every auspicious rite, who is a forest fire to the thickets of various karmas, who reveals the state of one's true nature, who is free from all conceptual constructions, who is the abode of all happiness, who cuts the root of manifold sufferings, and who is incomparably beautiful. 33.
